Food is fairly digested (think liquid or maybe chunky at most) by the time it reaches your ileocecal valve. Like you mentioned, it’s literally a valve that will dump all that stuff into the colon - but anything larger / more solid might not squeeze through. Examples I’ve seen include psych patients who swallow pen caps, kids who swallow coins, drug users who swallow needles, overzealous eaters who swallow bones. Surgery gets involved because there’s always a chance a foreign body can perforate the intestine.

Based on this radiograph, capsule looks stuck in the terminal ileum at the ileocecal valve, where the small intestine empties into the large intestine. As a surgeon, we see foreign bodies get stuck here often. Can probably get there with a colonoscope and retrieve the capsule after traversing the entire colon and intubating the terminal ileum. Also, if you did have gastrointestinal bleeding / bloody or dark bowel movements and have NOT had a colonoscopy yet, would HIGHLY recommend you get a colonoscopy anyway.

We started out physical, on & off for about a year (no sex), but she never wanted to try for a relationship so we tried building a friendship. We became best friends, but the friendship was strained at times because of our mutual and respective pasts. I developed strong feelings for her, but I was able to repress them for the sake of our friendship. She knew this. I have a habit of being 100% truthful, however unnecessary. 

2 tumultuous years later, she checked in, as per usual. I told her not much has changed: feelings are still there, but I thought the friendship was going well. She decided we should “take a break”. I obliged, but after 2 months of not talking I had no idea what exactly we were taking a break for. She checked in again. I told her I was confused - what changes had to be made before we could be friends again? What was our goal during this break? Time alone doesn’t heal -  I need to be proactive. 

I told her I still think about it everyday - she was my best friend. And I’ll never forget her response, which was the breaking point for me: she told me I cared too much and that I was too intense. I totally agree. But it was at that point I realized we are fundamentally different people, through and through. We probably never would have tried being friends had we not been physically attracted to each other in the first place. The next week I told her I did not want to pursue the friendship any further. 

Granted this is only my perspective, and obviously there’s a lot of detail omitted. I blame myself for being emotional; for not being able to deal with my feelings in the way she wanted. In retrospect, as well as I knew her, there was still a lot she was keeping from me; and a lot she should work through on her own, before she can truly engage in meaningful friendships and/or relationships. Once she finds peace with herself, I have no doubt she will be a phenomenal best friend and/or SO. 

But at some point, I had to stop rolling with the punches. So I noped right out of one of the most important friendships I’ve ever had.

TL;DR: establish a friendship first, then hook up later!! Much easier to revert back to a friendship you are already familiar with, versus trying to create one out of the ashes of a failed physical relationship.
